# Icons

Figma: [Icons](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-882)

Syntropy uses two icon styles. The primary set is Streamline Sharp Line - clean, geometric, single-stroke marks on a 24px grid, held in a separate published library (Syntropy Icons) subscribed to this design system. The second is isocons - isometric line illustrations for empty states and large status moments. This page documents both, plus sizing, colour tokens, alignment patterns, and how to extend the set for Saudi-specific concepts Streamline doesn’t cover.

## The Icon System

Syntropy uses Streamline Sharp Line for its icon system. Sharp Line is one of Streamline’s commercial icon families - single-stroke, geometric, but-cap, miter-joined marks built on a 24px grid. The "Sharp" in the name is literal: corners are sharp, stroke endings are sharp, the visual language is crisp and brutalist rather than friendly and rounded. This is the flat, inline icon style; for large isometric spot illustrations, see the Isometric Icons (Isocons) section below.

- Source: Streamline Sharp Line (5,616 icons, 24px grid, commercial license via Safqah's Streamline Pro account)
- Stroke weight: 1.5px at 24×24 (scales proportionally when icons are resized)
- Corners: sharp (miter join) - never round
- Stroke caps: but - never round
- Color: every icon's strokes are bound to the icon/default semantic token by default
Architecture · Separate Library File

Icons live in their own published Figma file ("Syntropy Icons") rather than inside this design system file. Syntropy DS subscribes to that library to get access to icon components. The icons file subscribes back to Syntropy DS for variable access (icon/default, icon/muted, etc.) - so colors propagate one-way from this file down to icons. This split keeps the design system file lean, lets icons update independently, and makes the icon set reusable across other Safqah projects.

## Sizing

Syntropy provides one icon component per icon, drawn at 24×24. To use an icon at another size, resize the component instance manually - Streamline Sharp Line scales proportionally, so the stroke weight adjusts with the size. Four sizes are sanctioned: 16, 20, 24, 32. Other sizes should be avoided unless there's a specific design reason.

> **Info:** Only one 24×24 component ships per icon. Resize manually for 16/20/32. We don't maintain separate components per size - this keeps the library smaller and avoids version drift. Engineers do the same in code: one source SVG resized via the size prop.

16px

Dense UI · inline with body text · table cells

20px

Compact UI · small buttons · list metadata

24px

DEFAULT · standard buttons · nav items · most UI

32px

Large CTAs · empty-state hints · feature highlights

## Color

Every icon ships with its strokes bound to icon/default - the default text-on-surface color. Designers override per-instance to express state or hierarchy. The icon color token system mirrors text tokens: default for primary, muted for secondary, brand for emphasis, status colors for feedback.

icon/default

Primary icon color - default binding for all icons

icon/muted

Secondary / less emphasis - captions, helper text

icon/subtle

Disabled / placeholder

icon/inverse

On dark surfaces

icon/brand/primary

Brand green emphasis - primary CTAs

icon/brand/darkest

Darker brand emphasis - focused / pressed

icon/success

Confirmation, completion, gains

icon/warning

Caution, pending review

icon/error

Errors, failures, losses

icon/info

Informational hints, tips

icon/progress

Status lines, status tabs

## Alignment with Text

Icons paired with text must align optically. The rule of thumb: match icon size to the line-height of the text, then center vertically. Streamline Sharp Line icons are designed to align cleanly to text baselines when sized 16/20/24 - the visual mass sits roughly on the x-height line.

Common pairings:

Account · 12,500 SAR

16px icon + body/13 - table cells, dense lists

Account · 12,500 SAR

20px icon + body/14 - compact list items, small buttons

My Wallet

24px icon + body/16 - standard buttons, nav, most UI

My Wallet

24px icon + heading/18 - section titles, page headers

Total Balance

32px icon + heading/22 - feature highlights, hero stats

> **Info:** In Arabic (RTL) mode, the icon sits to the RIGHT of the text, not the left. Auto-layout handles the swap automatically when you set the layout direction. Some icons also need to mirror visually - arrows, chevrons, and directional indicators. See "Working in RTL" in the notes section below for the full list.

## Beyond the Curated Set

The ~30 icons in the curated set cover most common needs. For anything else, designers have two sanctioned routes: Streamline’s Figma plugin (for any icon in the Sharp Line family - 5,616 total), and the community Lucide Figma library (subscribed alongside Syntropy Icons). Both produce icons compatible with the Syntropy colour tokens.

> **Tip:** Streamline Figma plugin: install once, search any of the 5,616 Sharp Line icons by name, drag onto canvas. After dropping in, rebind the icon's stroke to icon/default and rename it to Icon / [name] to match the convention. If an icon is used in production code, add it to the curated set so it lives in the Syntropy Icons library permanently.

> **Tip:** Lucide community library: useful when Streamline Sharp Line doesn't have an exact match. Lucide's rounded style is slightly different visually, so avoid mixing both in the same component or screen - pick one per context.

## Custom Icons - Safqah Extension

Some concepts unique to Saudi fintech aren't in any standard icon library: Sukuk certificate, Sharia compliance mark, Murabaha contract, specific real-estate categories, government identity systems (Abshir, Tawakkalna, Nafath). These belong to a small custom extension set drawn by Safqah's design team, following the same conventions as Streamline Sharp Line.

Rules for a custom Safqah icon to be accepted into the extension set:

- 24×24 grid, 1.5px stroke weight (matches Streamline Sharp Line scale)
- Sharp corners (miter join), butt stroke caps - never rounded
- Strokes bound to icon/default token (not raw colors)
- Single visual concept - no compound icons combining multiple metaphors
- Named Icon / safqah-[concept] (e.g. Icon / safqah-sukuk, Icon / safqah-sharia-mark) so they're distinguishable from Streamline icons
- Added to the published Syntropy Icons library file alongside Streamline icons
- Approved by the design system maintainer (you, Abdulrahman) before publishing

> **Warning:** Don't draw custom icons that already exist in Streamline Sharp Line. Use Streamline's search first - its 5,616-icon set is broader than it looks. Custom icons should only fill genuine gaps.

## Isometric Icons (Isocons)

Alongside the flat Streamline Sharp Line set, Syntropy ships a second, distinct icon style: isometric icons - "isocons". These are 3D single-stroke line illustrations drawn on an isometric grid, larger and more expressive than a 24px glyph, and used where a flat icon is too small to carry meaning.

Isocons live in the illustrations set (2071:38797 - 56 variants) and appear mainly in EmptyState, one isocon per deal or portfolio state. Each type ships in Left and Right alignment so the illustration can lean toward the copy.

- Style - isometric single-stroke line, multi-tone (ink + one accent). A separate style from the flat 24px Sharp Line glyphs; the two are never mixed in the same slot.
- ~28 semantic types mapped to deal & portfolio states - Active, Raising, Scheduled, Preparing, Repayment due, Matured, Defaulted, In recovery, and more.
- Alignment property (Left / Right) leans the illustration toward the adjacent copy - pick the side that faces the text.
- Use for empty states, onboarding, and large status moments. Never inline with body text - that is the flat icon’s role.
- Render at illustration scale (≈48–120px), keep the isometric angle. Don’t rotate, flatten, or recolor outside the defined tones.

> **Info:** Flat vs isocon - reach for a Sharp Line glyph for controls and inline meaning; reach for an isocon for whole-screen moments (empty states, success, onboarding).

- Illustration Library - isocon set (EmptyState 05d)

## Misuse

Common mistakes when using icons. The deeper anti-pattern discussion is in the Notes section below - these are the quick-glance rules.

> **Don't:** Don't scale icons non-uniformly. Resize by dragging a corner (proportional). Never stretch width or height alone - Sharp Line stroke weights stay consistent only with uniform scaling.

> **Don't:** Don't recolor icons manually. Use the icon/* tokens. A custom hex breaks theme switching and creates drift.

> **Don't:** Don't mix icon families in the same screen. Don't put Streamline Sharp Line and Lucide icons in the same component or view - their stroke styles clash visually.

> **Don't:** Don't use icons as pure decoration. Every icon should communicate something. Decorative icons clutter the interface and reduce the meaning of icons that actually do mean something.

## Code Reference

How engineers consume Syntropy icons in the Flutter codebase. The design system's icons are sourced from Streamline's public API + MCP server, so engineers and designers pull from the same canonical source.

Flutter (Safqah app)

// Icons are bundled as SVG assets in /assets/icons/streamline/sharp-line/
// Named identically to the Figma components: Icon / wallet → wallet.svg

import 'package:flutter_svg/flutter_svg.dart';
import 'package:safqah/theme/icon_tokens.dart';

SvgPicture.asset(
  'assets/icons/streamline/sharp-line/wallet.svg',
  width: 24,
  height: 24,
  colorFilter: ColorFilter.mode(
    IconTokens.defaultColor,  // matches icon/default in Figma
    BlendMode.srcIn,
  ),
)

// Or via the SafqahIcon wrapper (preferred):
SafqahIcon(
  name: 'wallet',
  size: 24,
  color: IconTokens.defaultColor,  // optional, defaults to icon/default
)

> **Tip:** Engineers and designers should pull from the same canonical Streamline source. When a new icon enters the curated set, it's added to both the Syntropy Icons Figma file AND the Flutter assets directory in the same PR. Don't let the two drift.

### Why icons matter

Icons are the densest form of communication in an interface. A single 24×24 glyph can convey "wallet," "secure," "in progress," or "delete" faster than any word. Users scan an interface before they read it - and icons are the anchors that tell them where to look, what's actionable, and what means what.

In a financial product, this density matters even more. A user opening Safqah's wallet screen needs to identify their balance, their transactions, their investment status, and their action affordances in under a second. If the icons are inconsistent - different stroke weights, different visual styles, different metaphors - the cognitive load increases and the interface feels amateur. Consistent icons signal "this team paid attention to the details," which in fintech is the same as signaling "this team can be trusted with my money."

Streamline Sharp Line was chosen specifically because its visual character - sharp, geometric, brutalist - communicates seriousness over playfulness. The same icon set in Lucide's rounded style would feel friendlier but less authoritative. For an Arabic-first Saudi fintech product, sharp geometric icons sit better next to Arabic typography's natural geometric character than rounded forms do.

### Choosing the right icon

Icon selection is one of the most underrated parts of interface design. The wrong icon doesn't just look bad - it actively misleads. A user who sees a "save" icon expects saving, not exporting. Trust gets damaged every time a metaphor breaks.

| Col 1 | Col 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Pick the most recognized metaphor, not the most clever one | A floppy disk for "save" feels dated, but it's universally understood. A custom drawing of a cloud with a checkmark is novel but slower to parse. In product UI, recognition beats novelty almost every time. |
| Match the icon to the action, not the object | For a "transfer money" button, prefer an arrow-exchange icon (the action) over a wallet icon (the object). Users scan for verbs in interfaces - the icon should reinforce the verb. |
| Saudi cultural context matters | Some Western icons don't translate well. A piggy-bank icon for "savings" is fine in the US but culturally inappropriate in Saudi Arabia (pigs being haram). A vault, a coin stack, or a wallet works better. Always check icons against the local context. |
| When in doubt, use text instead | If you can't find an icon that clearly communicates a concept, don't force one. A clear text label is always better than an ambiguous icon. Icons should reduce reading effort, not add to it. |

> **Tip:** Run a 5-second test: show the screen to someone unfamiliar with it for 5 seconds, then ask them what's on it. If they can't describe what icons mean from glance alone, the icons are working against you, not for you.

### Working in RTL (Arabic mode)

Safqah is an Arabic-first product. When the interface flips to Arabic, the layout direction reverses - but icons don't all behave the same way. Some need to mirror, some stay identical. Getting this right is the difference between a polished Arabic experience and one that feels translated.

| Col 1 | Col 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Icons that MUST mirror in Arabic | Directional indicators: arrows, chevrons, "back" buttons, progress flows, send/receive icons, "next/previous" navigation. These all flip horizontally because the reading direction is reversed. Examples: arrow-right becomes arrow-left, chevron-right becomes chevron-left, etc. |
| Icons that MUST NOT mirror | Symbolic/iconographic glyphs whose meaning doesn't depend on direction: clock, eye, heart, lock, key, calendar, search, star, user, settings. These look identical in any language. Mirroring them looks wrong. |
| Icons with text inside (avoid these) | Icons that contain letters or numbers (badges with "1", "A", "$") shouldn't mirror - but ideally you shouldn't use them at all in a bilingual product. The text gets stretched or rotated incorrectly during mirroring. Replace with a textless icon plus a separate text element. |
| Implementation in Flutter | Flutter's Directionality widget handles most of this automatically when you wrap your icons in a Directionality-aware widget like Icon. For SafqahIcon (the custom wrapper), pass mirrorInRTL: true for directional icons and false for symbolic ones. Default is false - meaning you have to explicitly mark which icons mirror. |

> **Warning:** Don't mirror icons via the auto-layout flip-on-RTL trick alone. That mirrors EVERYTHING in the icon, including text/numbers if present, and produces broken visuals. Use the dedicated mirrorInRTL prop on each icon component.

### Accessibility

Icons can either help accessibility or hurt it, depending on how they're used. The rules below apply to both Figma designs and Flutter code.

| Col 1 | Col 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum tap target: 44×44 | Icons themselves can be 24×24, but the tappable area around them must be at least 44×44 (Apple/Google standard). For an Icon Button, that means a 44×44 button with a 24×24 icon centered inside. |
| Don't rely on color alone | If an icon's meaning depends on its color (red for danger, green for success), reinforce with shape or text. Color-blind users miss a quarter of "red vs green" distinctions. The icon shape itself should carry the meaning - a check-circle is success regardless of color. |
| Semantic vs decorative - handle differently in code | Meaningful icons (the only label for an action) need aria-label or semanticLabel in Flutter. Decorative icons (paired with explicit text) should have semanticLabel: "" to prevent screen readers from announcing them twice. |
| Contrast | Icon strokes need 3:1 contrast against their background per WCAG 2.1 non-text contrast. The icon/default token meets this on bg/surface. If you use icon colors on unusual backgrounds (an icon on a brand-green button, e.g.), check the pairing manually with a contrast checker. |

> **Tip:** When designing, ask: "If I removed this icon, would the user still understand the screen?" If yes, the icon is decorative - keep it but mark it as such in code. If no, the icon is semantic - make sure it has a label.

### The Streamline Sharp Line system

Sharp Line is one of about a dozen Streamline icon families. The choice of this specific family shapes how the entire Safqah product feels - so it's worth understanding what makes it different from the alternatives.

| Col 1 | Col 2 |
| --- | --- |
| 5,616 icons, 24px grid, 1.5px stroke | The full family covers most fintech UI needs. The 24px grid is the modern web standard. The 1.5px stroke at 24×24 scales down cleanly to 1px at 16×16 and up to 2px at 32×32 without visual breakage. |
| Sharp vs other Streamline families | Streamline Core has slightly rounded corners and friendlier endings. Streamline Plump is heavier. Streamline Solar is filled. Streamline Sharp is the most geometric and brutalist - straight lines, sharp corners, no decorative touches. Best for serious products. |
| Why not Material Symbols or SF Symbols? | Material Symbols are tied to Google's aesthetic. SF Symbols are Apple-specific (license-restricted outside Apple platforms). Streamline is platform-neutral and license-flexible. For a cross-platform fintech product, platform-neutral matters. |
| License and renewal | Safqah holds a Streamline Pro subscription that covers all families including Sharp Line. The license needs renewal annually. If the subscription lapses, existing downloaded icons remain usable but new icons cannot be pulled. Renewal responsibility sits with the design team. |

### Anti-patterns (Don't do this)

Recurring mistakes when working with icons. Each one degrades the system in a way that's hard to undo later.

> **Don't:** Don't use icons without color tokens. Hardcoded hex values break theme switching and create silent drift between Figma and code. Always bind to icon/* tokens.

> **Don't:** Don't introduce a new icon style for "one screen only." Designers under deadline pressure will reach for whatever icon they can find - Material, Font Awesome, an icon from another product's screenshot. Once it ships, it's in the codebase forever.

> **Don't:** Don't use icons inside icons (nested compound icons). A wallet icon with a small plus icon stuck on it to mean "add to wallet" looks clever in design but reads as cluttered noise at 24×24 in production.

> **Don't:** Don't scale icons below 16px. At 12-14px, Sharp Line strokes get too thin to render reliably across devices. Stick to the 16/20/24/32 scale.

> **Don't:** Don't put colored icons on colored buttons without checking contrast. A green icon on a green button fails accessibility. The icon/inverse token exists specifically for this case - use it on brand-colored backgrounds.

> **Don't:** Don't reuse the same icon for different actions in the same screen. If "settings" and "preferences" both use a cog icon, users can't tell them apart. Pick distinct icons or rename one.

> **Don't:** Don't add icons "just to fill space." If a button feels empty without an icon, the button is probably too wide. Don't use icons as visual padding.
